company.name: Flow Engineering
company.tagline: Synchronizes model-based engineering teams' data, enabling them to bring their products to market faster
company.about:
Flow Engineering, founded in 2016 by CEO Pari Singh, operates as a collaboration platform for hardware engineering teams, often described as the "GitHub for hardware". The company, with locations in London and Los Angeles, was established to address inefficiencies in traditional hardware development. Singh, motivated by a desire to solve significant global challenges like climate change through engineering, initially co-founded a rapid-prototyping rocket engine design consultancy. This experience of accelerating hardware design from weeks to a fraction of the time by building custom automation tools revealed a broader market need. The company pivoted from hardware to a software-as-a-service (SaaS) model to provide these collaboration tools to the wider engineering community. 

The firm targets 'new age' hardware engineering teams in sectors such as space, defense, transportation, robotics, and clean energy, including nuclear and fusion technologies. Its client base includes companies that represent a significant portion of the world's orbital payload mass. Flow Engineering generates revenue through its SaaS platform, which helps companies reduce time-to-market by 30-50%. The business model is structured to streamline the entire engineering design framework, from requirements to verification, reducing the substantial time engineers spend on data administration. 

The core offering is a cloud-based platform that acts as a single source of truth for complex engineering projects. It provides an agile requirements management tool that facilitates collaboration, design iteration, and verification. Key features include tools for document collaboration, version control, project sharing, live V&V (Verification and Validation) tracking, and workflow analysis. The platform integrates with existing engineering tools like GitHub and CAD software, allowing for the parameterization of text-based requirements into machine-readable checks. This system is designed to give engineers ownership of requirements and foster a systems-first mindset, ultimately accelerating the design and verification processes to prevent costly delays. Deployment options are flexible, including cloud SaaS, AWS GovCloud, or self-hosted setups to meet various security and compliance standards like ITAR and EAR.

company.name: Occam
company.tagline: GPS-independent autonomy software for unmanned systems
company.about:
Occam Industries is a London-based defense technology firm founded in 2025 by Gui Wainwright. The company specializes in developing software for unmanned systems, such as drones, enabling them to operate autonomously without reliance on GPS or external communications. 

The core product, OccamX, is a retrofit computer-vision autopilot designed for mass-manufactured first-person-view (FPV) drones. This software-only solution can be integrated into existing drone platforms without needing to alter the airframe or supply chains. By using computer vision for perception, tracking, and guidance, the technology reduces the need for continuous manual control from a human operator and lowers the required skill level. This addresses a key challenge in modern warfare where drone pilots are scarce resources and vulnerable to being targeted. The system is designed to be immune to electronic warfare and signal loss, allowing drone missions to be completed in contested environments where human-piloted systems cannot operate. 

Occam Industries operates on a B2B and B2G business model, licensing its software to defense manufacturers and government programs. The company has established a significant partnership with Ukraine's Brave1 defense tech cluster, which approved the technology for integration testing. This collaboration involves deploying the technology with Ukrainian unmanned system manufacturers, using the active conflict as a demanding operational environment to test and refine the software's latency, reliability, and decision-making capabilities. Beyond Ukraine, Occam is pursuing paid adoption projects and strategic partnerships with European defense primes to enhance NATO capabilities. 

In February 2026, Occam Industries secured €3 million in a pre-seed funding round. The round was led by Presto Tech Horizons and included participation from Antler, Freedom Fund, TYR.vc, and other angel investors. This capital is intended to accelerate the adoption of its technology on the Ukrainian front line, expand the system's capabilities, and advance product development.

company.name: Basecamp Research
company.tagline: AI protein and therapeutic design from biodiversity-scale genomic data
company.about: Basecamp Research is a London biotechnology company founded in 2019 by Dr Glen Gowers and Dr Oliver Vince that trains foundational biological AI models on proprietary genomic data collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries. Its knowledge graph and BaseData protein corpus underpin the Eden model family for protein and DNA sequence design, including BaseFold structure prediction and aiPGI for programmable gene insertion, with a therapeutic focus on in vivo cell therapy that aims to reprogram patient cells inside the body. The company collaborates with pharmaceutical, research and industrial partners and cites preclinical progress across multiple disease areas. Funding includes a $20 million Series A (2022) and $60 million Series B (2024); in September 2026 Basecamp closed a $140 million Series C led by S32, with NVentures (NVIDIA), Anthropic’s Anthology Fund, Catalio, the NATO Innovation Fund, Rockefeller, European Tech Collective, the UK Sovereign AI Fund and returning investors Firebrand, River Capital King Philanthropies and Redalpine — bringing total funding to about $225 million to train next-generation models and advance AI-designed therapeutics toward the clinic. company.name: FAT32
company.tagline: Compliance in minutes, not months
company.about:
FAT32 Ltd, operating under the brand name OneClickComply, is a Sunderland-based company specializing in cybersecurity and regulatory compliance automation. The company was founded by Connor Greig, Conor Sizeland, and David Warren, who combined their expertise in software engineering and cybersecurity to address the complexities of regulatory adherence. Connor Greig serves as the CEO. The firm was established in 2024 and operates within the Software as a Service (SaaS) sector. 

The company's primary offering is the OneClickComply platform, an all-in-one security, trust, and compliance solution. This platform is designed to simplify and automate the process for businesses of all sizes to meet various regulatory standards, including ISO 27001, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials, and CIS v8. It serves businesses across different sectors that need to adhere to increasingly stringent cyber and information security regulations. The business model appears to be subscription-based, offering significant cost and time savings compared to manual compliance processes or hiring external consultants. 

The core of the product is its automation capability, which not only identifies compliance gaps but also auto-implements the necessary technical controls and remediations with a single click, a feature branded as 'OneClickFix'. This can reduce compliance timelines from months to weeks. The platform also features 'AutoComplete Policies' for automatically generating IT and security policies based on real-time system configurations, continuous 24/7 monitoring to ensure ongoing compliance, and a 'Trust Centre' that provides real-time access to compliance information for customers and their auditors. Additional services include vendor risk management, vulnerability management, and penetration testing solutions. 

FAT32 Ltd has demonstrated significant growth, having secured over £1.2 million in investment through multiple funding rounds. A recent round in August 2025 raised £580,000 from investors including Northstar Ventures, angel investors, and a grant from Innovate UK. This capital is intended to support software development, team expansion, and solidify the company's presence in the North East's cybersecurity cluster.

company.name: Stasher
company.tagline: Global luggage storage network for travelers
company.about:
Stasher is a luggage storage network that connects travelers with hotels and local businesses with available space to store their bags. Founded in 2015 by Jacob Wedderburn-Day, Anthony Collias, and Matthew Majewski, the company originated from a joke when Collias's friends asked to store luggage at his apartment near King's Cross station in London. This sparked the idea for a formal service, initially called CityStasher. 

The founders, who met while studying at the University of Oxford, developed a prototype while completing their studies. They secured their first investment after sending a cold email to James Gibson, the CEO of Big Yellow Storage. Stasher operates on a peer-to-peer model, often described as the "Airbnb of luggage," allowing travelers to book storage space online for short-term needs. This is particularly useful for those with gaps between accommodation check-outs and flight departures or for day-trippers. The service is accessible via a mobile-optimized website and an app where users can find and book a "StashPoint" in over 1,000 cities across 75 countries. The business model involves Stasher taking a commission of around 50% from the storage fee, with the remainder going to the host business, which also benefits from increased foot traffic. 

Since its launch, the company has achieved significant milestones, including being recognized in Forbes' "30 under 30" list for Europe in 2020. Stasher has raised a total of $3.72 million over four funding rounds, including a $2.5 million seed round in January 2020 led by VentureFriends. This funding has supported global expansion and the formation of partnerships with major travel and hospitality brands like Hotels.com, Klook, Marriott, Accor, and Premier Inn. In June 2024, Stasher acquired its US competitor, StoreMe, to expand its footprint in the American market. The company has also acquired other international players such as Airkeep.me in Latin America and MindMyBag.com in Australia and New Zealand. 

The service offers a flat fee per bag per day, with no size restrictions, and includes insurance coverage for each item stored. Stasher has expanded its offerings by integrating with postal locker networks, providing another convenient storage option for customers. The company focuses on trust and security, vetting all host locations and maintaining a high customer satisfaction rating. In early 2026, Stasher announced a partnership with Victoria Coach Station, the UK's busiest coach terminal, to become its official online luggage storage provider.

company.name: Mozilla Data Collective
company.tagline: AI data-sharing platform for human agency.
company.about: Mozilla Data Collective is a UK mission-locked social enterprise that runs a consent-first marketplace for AI training data, letting communities and organisations share multilingual, multicultural and multimodal datasets while retaining ownership, setting licenses and—when they choose—charging for compensated access. Founded and led by CEO E.M. Lewis-Jong and incubated by the Mozilla Foundation (spinning out of Common Voice and the Data Futures Lab), it launched publicly in November 2025 and became a standalone British company in 2026; downloaders pay a 5% platform fee while uploaders keep 100% of any license fees they set. The curated catalogue spans more than 450 languages with hundreds of vetted contributing organisations, serving major AI labs, startups and scale-ups under EU AI Act-style provenance expectations. Features include Compensated Datasets, request-to-access controls and tools for builders to find and request data. In September 2026 Mozilla Data Collective raised $5 million from Mozilla to expand multimodal cultural video and large text corpora across EU, African and South Asian languages, add startup-friendly licensing, and bring R&D Lab security and data-improvement capabilities onto the platform. Sources: MarTech Series / Business Wire 21 Sep 2026; Mozilla Data Collective community.

company.name: Azoma
company.tagline: AI platform for e-commerce generative engine optimization
company.about:
Azoma.ai, also known as Ecomtent Inc., provides an enterprise-grade Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) platform designed to enhance brand visibility within AI-powered search engines. The company's core service revolves around helping brands track their presence, generate optimized content, and increase their share of voice on platforms like ChatGPT, Amazon Rufus, Google AI Overviews, and Perplexity. The platform offers solutions for both brands and retailers, including analytics on AI conversations, consumer trend insights, and the generation of optimized product listings with visual and written content. For retailers, it focuses on automating e-commerce merchandising at scale by creating content that aims to improve conversion and discoverability. 

Azoma was co-founded in 2022 by CEO Max Sinclair and CTO Timur Leguev. Sinclair's background includes six years at Amazon, where he was involved in search, catalog quality, and the launch of Amazon Singapore. This experience provided him with insights into the challenges and future of product search, which led to the creation of Azoma after he was introduced to early models of GPT-3. Leguev is a PhD and Fulbright Scholar with over ten years of experience in AI research and has founded other AI startups. The company is backed by investors including MaRS IAF, Twinpath, Techstars, and eBay Ventures. 

The company's platform addresses the shift from traditional SEO to GEO, as consumers increasingly use AI chatbots for product research. Its technology allows brands to generate thousands of product listings, including lifestyle images and infographics, that are optimized for discoverability and conversion. Azoma offers integrations with e-commerce platforms like Shopify and Walmart and provides analytics to track metrics such as response accuracy, citation frequency, and sentiment in AI-generated responses. The company serves clients like Canadian Tire, Zappos, and Ruroc, reporting significant increases in brand mentions and conversion rates for its customers.

company.name: Magentic
company.tagline: AI digital workers for industrial procurement and supply-chain operations
company.about:
Magentic builds AI digital workers for procurement and supply-chain operations at large industrial manufacturers. Its multi-agent systems work inside tools teams already use—Microsoft Teams, email and internal enterprise systems—to run workflows end-to-end, from buy-versus-build decisions and supplier selection to contract negotiation, order management and invoice processing, across both indirect and direct spend. Founded in 2025 by CEO Robin Van Aeken and CTO Odhran O'Donoghue and based in London and New York, Magentic targets Global 500 manufacturers facing rising procurement workloads, tariff pressure and fragmented legacy systems. In September 2026 it raised an $18 million Series A led by Felicis, with participation from existing investors Sequoia Capital and The Westly Group, following a $5.5 million Seed. The capital expands agent coverage across procurement and supply-chain workflows and deepens long-horizon AI research for complex industrial optimisation.

Sources: Magentic (17 Sep 2026); Tech.eu (17 Sep 2026).

company.name: Eterna Regeneratives
company.tagline: Keratin biomaterials for tooth enamel and bone regeneration
company.about: Eterna Regeneratives is a London biotechnology spin-out from King's College London founded in 2024 by Khaled Eissa (CEO) and Dr Sherif Elsharkawy (CSO) that builds a keratin-based regenerative biomaterials platform. Its patented material, derived from sheep's wool keratin, is designed to stimulate mineralisation that regrows damaged tooth enamel—unlike fluoride, which only strengthens existing enamel, or resin fillings that patch rather than rebuild—and early work also points to bone-regeneration applications. In vitro tests on extracted teeth showed enamel-like layers with hardness approaching healthy enamel. In September 2026 Eterna closed a $4 million Seed co-led by Hoxton Ventures and The Venture Collective to move from lab proof-of-concept to commercial oral-care products (e.g. toothpaste formats), expand research and commercial teams in Canary Wharf, and pursue partnerships across the estimated $43 billion global oral-care market. Sources: PR Newswire 17 Sep 2026; Startup.eu; eternaregeneratives.co.

company.name: AcouBatt
company.tagline: Acoustic AI diagnostics for safer, faster battery manufacturing
company.about:
AcouBatt is a London deeptech startup spun out of UCL Ventures that uses acoustic emission sensing and AI to diagnose battery cells during manufacturing and operation. Founded in 2025 by Dr Arthur Fordham (CEO; PhD research at UCL’s Electrochemical Innovation Lab / Faraday Institution SafeBatt) and Chris Haoxin Xu (Commercial Director), the company monitors processes inside lithium-ion cells in real time — especially during formation, when manufacturers often lack visibility into cell state.

By combining acoustic and electrochemical signals, AcouBatt aims to detect when formation is complete (potentially cutting formation time by up to 30%), spot faults and process deviations before a batch finishes, and later extend diagnostics to battery energy storage systems and other battery-powered applications. Sensors are deployed at the UK Battery Industrialisation Centre (UKBIC) for industrial benchmarking ahead of commercial roll-out.

In September 2026 AcouBatt raised £1.1 million pre-seed led by Creator Fund with Ada Ventures to expand the technical team, advance AI models and industrial pilots with battery manufacturers. Sources: Tech.eu 16 Sep 2026; acoubatt.ai.

company.name: Quartz
company.tagline: Personal finance app with an AI banker for everyday investors
company.about:
Quartz is a London fintech founded in 2025 by former Revolut Head of Global Expansion André Silva (CEO) and former N26 Investment Product Lead Mateus Mesquita Alves, building a personal finance platform that consolidates pensions, ISAs, savings and investments in one app and pairs them with personalised guidance.

Registered with the UK Financial Conduct Authority as an Account Information Service Provider, Quartz uses proprietary connectors to bring products into a single view and offers Charlie, an AI assistant that draws on the user’s finances and market developments to surface insights and answer questions. The product targets the gap between high-cost personalised wealth advice and standardised products with little individual guidance. After testing from Q1 2026, Quartz reported more than £10 million in members’ assets tracked and is onboarding waitlist users in batches; the app is on the App Store and Google Play.

In September 2026 Quartz raised £2.75 million pre-seed led by Daphni, with Outward VC, K Fund and angels including Kantox founder Philippe Gelis and former N26/Kraken CPO Gilles BianRosa. The company cites a ~10-person team across London, Barcelona and Porto. Sources: Tech.eu 16 Sep 2026; myquartz.ai.

company.name: AcademyAI
company.tagline: AI skill assessment and role-specific workplace training
company.about:
AcademyAI is a UK workplace-AI skills company that helps organisations measure whether employees can use AI tools effectively and close the gap between tool adoption and real outcomes. Co-founded by Alex Packham, Andy Lambert, Michael Walton and Rob Barnett, the platform assesses people on a six-axis AI capability framework developed with Alan Turing Institute methodology — covering areas such as critical thinking, judgement, prompting, evaluating AI outputs and practical application — then delivers role-specific learning.

Instead of long generic webinars, AcademyAI serves short (~five-minute) applied modules tailored to an organisation’s tools, terminology and workflows, and uses underlying AI models to refresh content as practices evolve. Managers get dashboards tracking capability progress across individuals, teams and departments, plus reassessment and certification paths. The product is tool-agnostic and aimed at knowledge-worker organisations rolling out assistants such as ChatGPT and Copilot.

In September 2026 AcademyAI raised an oversubscribed £1.65 million pre-seed from Nexus Family Office and Panthera Family Office to further develop assessment and role-specific training as workplace AI adoption scales. Sources: Tech.eu 15 Sep 2026; academyai.co.

company.name: OriginalVoices
company.tagline: Human-generated digital twins that give AI real-time audience opinions and preferences.
company.about:
OriginalVoices is a London-based platform that supplies human-generated data and insights for AI systems and agents. Rather than synthetic audiences or AI-generated personas, it builds a network of one-to-one digital twins, each linked to and managed by a real person, so AI tools can query what people currently think and feel about topics, products, brands and services. Twins can be accessed through AI tools including ChatGPT and Claude, and via the Twineo consumer app, through which people create, train and manage their digital twins. Since launching Twineo in December 2025, the company reports tens of thousands of digital twin profiles. It has also partnered with YouGov on YouGov Parallax, combining YouGov panel data with OriginalVoices’ twin infrastructure. Co-founded by CEO David Dobrin, OriginalVoices raised a £1 million pre-seed round led by Iona Star in September 2026 to scale the team, expand the twin network and product offering, and grow in the US.

Sources: Tech.eu (15 Sep 2026); originalvoices.ai.

company.name: Africa Global Trade Finance
company.tagline: Bespoke, secured trade finance solutions for Africa.
company.about: Africa Global Trade Finance (AGTF) is a non-bank financial institution founded in 2016 to facilitate trade and economic development in Africa. The company operates with a transaction-driven model, focusing on providing short-term, secured, and structured trade finance solutions for businesses engaged in trade to and from the African continent, with a particular emphasis on Sub-Saharan Africa. AGTF was established by the Africa Merchant Capital Group and is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, with additional offices in South Africa, Mauritius, and Singapore. The firm primarily serves small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), commodity importers, exporters, and traders who may be overlooked by traditional finance providers. Its client profile typically includes businesses with a trading history of over three years and a turnover of at least $5 million. A significant portion of its portfolio is dedicated to the agrifood sector, supporting food security and agricultural product trade. AGTF's financing is transactional, with terms generally ranging from 30 to 180 days, and is self-liquidating through the sale of goods. The company's methodology is designed to work in parallel with clients' existing banking relationships without interfering with bank collateral. This approach helps partner banks manage capital adequacy requirements under Basel III while continuing to serve their customers. In 2021, AGTF was acquired by the impact investment fund Zebu Investment Partners. The company has received significant investment from the Africa Food Security Fund and its manager, Exeo Capital, with total investment reaching approximately $20 million by September 2026. These capital injections are aimed at expanding AGTF's loan book, which stood at around $80 million in September 2026 with projections to exceed $200 million within two years. The leadership team includes Henno Loots, who was appointed acting CEO in February 2026, and a board that features members from its investment partners. The former CEO, Anne-Marie Woolley, a veteran with over 40 years in African trade finance, stepped down in February 2026. company.name: verifiedx.io
company.tagline: Bitcoin-native layer-1 financial network enabling payments, DeFi,and self-custodial financial applications for Bitcoin holders.
company.about:
VerifiedX is a layer-1 blockchain network purpose-built to turn Bitcoin into programmable financial capital. It operates as a Bitcoin-specific sidechain where Bitcoin is deposited and minted into vBTC, a fully collateralized and non-synthetic token that unlocks lending, yield, payments,and settlement use cases while preserving self-custody. The network's self-custodial architecture includes native wallets, social payment apps, on-chain payments and settlement,and a privacy layer that enables confidential transactions through zero-knowledge proofs. It serves retail users, institutions,and developers, with integrated on- and off-ramps via partners such as Crypto.com. Developers can build financial tools, marketplaces,and decentralized applications on top of the network. VerifiedX operates as a decentralized network with validator governance,and a native asset, VFX,that powers fees, liquidity,and governance, with network fees burned under a deflationary model. It targets institutions with integrated compliance,and AML risk-monitoring tooling, while keeping consumer-facing applications self-custodial,and free of central control. Applications built on the network include payments, DeFi,and tokenized AI agents, serving the emerging agentic economy.

Keywords: blockchain, Bitcoin, decentralized finance, crypto payments, self-custody, wallets, privacy, digital assets, layer 1, fintech.

company.name: Anemo Labs
company.tagline: AI electronic nose digitising smell for early disease screening
company.about:
Anemo Labs (formerly OdorPi) is a London deep-tech biotech startup building an AI-powered electronic nose that digitises smell for non-invasive disease screening. Founded in 2025 by Koye Sodipo, the team combines bespoke sensor chemistry and machine learning to detect disease-related volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in urine, aiming to flag conditions such as urinary tract infections and certain cancers before symptoms appear.

An in-house sampling platform can collect and label up to 5,000 smell samples a day to train models. In early Sniffin' Sticks protocol tests the company reported ~84% categorisation accuracy across about a dozen scent types. Current work focuses on sensor chemistry, expanding labelled datasets and clinical validation with partners.

In September 2026 Anemo Labs raised £700,000 pre-seed led by Zinc and SFC Capital, with Innovate UK support, to advance hardware, AI models and clinical evidence. Sources: Startupmag 9 Sep 2026; anemolabs.com.

company.name: Feisty
company.tagline: Plant-powered protein soda with no added sugar
company.about:
Feisty is a UK-based beverage company that has developed what it markets as the world's first plant-powered protein soda. The company was founded in 2024 by the mother-daughter team of Vy Cutting and her mother, Dr. Hong. The idea originated from Cutting's personal experience; following two knee surgeries, the former Louis Vuitton designer took up strength training but was dissatisfied with the taste and texture of existing protein shakes. This led to the creation of a soda that combines the refreshment of a fizzy drink with the benefits of protein. Dr. Hong, a scientist with a background in Microbiology and Chemistry, developed the patent-pending formula over 18 months, which enables pea protein to be dissolved in a clear, carbonated beverage without the typical gritty texture or aftertaste. 

Feisty's core product is a sparkling protein drink that contains 10 grams of complete plant-based protein per 330ml can, equivalent to the protein in two eggs. The protein is sourced from hydrolyzed pea and rice protein. The drinks are formulated to be clean-label, featuring no added sugar, low calories, and an absence of artificial sweeteners, flavors, or preservatives. The company primarily targets a broader audience than traditional protein products, with a particular focus on female consumers. Feisty operates on a direct-to-consumer model through its website and also sells its products through high-end retailers. Since its launch in March 2024, the brand has secured distribution in prominent UK stores such as Selfridges, Harrods, Whole Foods Market, and Soho House.

company.name: ARC Ride
company.tagline: Pioneering electric mobility in Africa by providing affordable, reliable, and clean transportation solutions through its battery-swapping network
company.about:
ARC Ride, standing for Affordable, Reliable, and Clean, is an electric mobility company established in 2019 with a strategic focus on electrifying the mass-transportation sector in rapidly growing African cities. Founded by CEO Joseph Hurst, a long-time investor and researcher in clean energy, the company is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, where it locally assembles its electric vehicles. The founding team, which includes Bede Hesmondhalgh, was driven by the goal of transitioning Kenya's transport system to a more cost-effective and environmentally sound model.

The company operates on a Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) business model, which is pivotal to its strategy of lowering the entry barrier for electric vehicle adoption. This model separates the cost of the vehicle from the cost of the battery, which is a significant portion of the upfront expense. Revenue is generated primarily through battery swaps. Riders can opt for a standard swap for approximately KES 185 or choose an unlimited daily swap plan for around KES 350, paid via mobile money integration like M-PESA. This structure offers an estimated 40% cost saving per kilometer compared to petrol-powered motorcycles, directly increasing the daily earnings of riders.

ARC Ride's core market consists of commercial motorcycle taxi operators, known as "boda boda" riders, in Kenya's urban centers, as well as corporate clients in the delivery and courier sectors. The company has deployed an extensive network of automated battery swapping cabinets across Nairobi, which it reports as the largest in East Africa. These IoT-enabled stations allow riders to exchange a depleted battery for a fully charged one in under a minute through a QR code-based mobile app, ensuring minimal downtime. The company also partners with local businesses to host these swap stations, creating an additional revenue stream for the partners.

The product ecosystem includes a range of electric two-wheelers, such as the "Corbett" model, which features a 3kW motor, a 200kg payload capacity, and a 60km range on a single charge. These vehicles are designed and assembled in-house. The swappable LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) smart batteries are lightweight and embedded with IoT chips for remote monitoring and performance management. Recent developments include a significant $5 million financing deal from British International Investment (BII) in May 2025, aimed at deploying 5,000 new electric motorcycles and further expanding the battery-swapping infrastructure.

company.name: Veridue
company.tagline: AI-native due diligence and M&A for energy infrastructure
company.about:
Veridue is a London-based AI-native due diligence and M&A platform purpose-built for energy infrastructure and data centres. Founded in 2024 by former McKinsey energy investment advisor Daniel Csonth (CEO) and former SCOR data science lead Xander van den Eelaart (CTO), the company accelerates investment and project financing for investors, independent power producers (IPPs), developers, lenders and insurers.

The platform helps buyers screen more opportunities, identify higher-quality assets and complete diligence faster — combining frontier AI models with a proprietary deterministic agent layer trained across thousands of risk factors, plus in-house energy transaction specialists who validate outputs. Capabilities include deal pipeline management, priority recommendations against investment criteria, automated red-flag diligence, document traceability and investment-readiness tooling for sellers (organised data rooms, VDD-style outputs and teasers).

After roughly two years of development with renewables and data-centre developers and investors, Veridue publicly launched on 8 September 2026 supported by a $4 million pre-seed round led by Episode 1 Ventures, with HTGF and Pi Labs, plus angels including Aurora Energy Research co-founder Cameron Hepburn and former QuantumBlack CEO Jeremy Palmer. Sources: veridue.ai launch blog 8 Sep 2026.

Sources: Startup.eu 16 Sep 2026; henneth.ai.

company.name: Triver
company.tagline: AI invoice financing and cashflow streaming for UK SMEs
company.about: Triver is a London fintech founded in 2022 by CEO Jerome Le Luel that provides working-capital funding for UK SMEs by advancing cash against unpaid invoices. Using Open Banking data and AI underwriting, Triver lets businesses set up a facility in minutes and fund an invoice in under five minutes, charging a single discount fee with no setup, interest or exit fees. An API-first embedded-finance model integrates with accounting platforms, digital banks and procurement tools (including Xero, Clear Books, Soldo, Elcom and Tide) so partners can offer cashflow at the point of need. Triver has financed tens of thousands of invoices for more than a thousand SME clients and holds substantial debt facilities alongside equity. In August 2026 it raised an additional £8 million Series B equity led by Calderwood Capital with existing investors, taking total VC equity to about £30 million to scale Cashflow Streaming and embedded partnerships. Sources: Triver blog 27 Aug 2026; Osborne Clarke.

company.name: Flip Therapeutics LTD
company.tagline: In vivo immune cell reprogramming for curative therapies.
company.about:
Flip Therapeutics LTD is a biotechnology company founded in 2024 and headquartered in London, United Kingdom. The company is focused on developing curative therapies for inflammatory and autoimmune diseases by utilizing in vivo cellular reprogramming to rebalance the immune system. 

The company was co-founded by Dave Pajerowski, PhD, who serves as CEO, Mathias Pawlak, PhD, the Chief Scientific Officer, and Anis Gammage, DPhil. Pajerowski has nearly 15 years of experience in biotechnology, previously holding leadership roles at Repertoire Immune Medicines and Nvelop Therapeutics, and contributing to the development of Moderna's Personalized Cancer Vaccine. Pawlak is an experienced immunologist and molecular biologist. 

Flip Therapeutics' core technology aims to reprogram pathogenic T cells, which are responsible for tissue destruction in many autoimmune diseases, into anti-inflammatory cells directly within the affected tissue. This approach is designed to both reduce inflammation and increase the suppressive capacity of the immune system locally. The company's method involves using proprietary payloads encoded in messenger RNA (mRNA) and delivered via lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology. This in vivo reprogramming seeks to overcome the limitations of current treatments, which often involve broad immunosuppression and significant side effects, by restoring the immune system's natural balance. 

By engineering immune cells directly within the body, Flip Therapeutics aims to create durable and potentially curative outcomes for patients with T cell-driven immune disorders such as multiple sclerosis, type 1 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. This strategy avoids the complex and costly manufacturing processes associated with ex vivo cell therapies, where cells are removed, modified in a lab, and then reinfused into the patient. The company is currently operating in stealth mode and received accelerator/incubator funding in February 2025.

company.name: Healthxchange Group
company.tagline: Aesthetic medical product distribution and clinician training
company.about:
Founded in 2000 by Dr. John Curran, Healthxchange Group is a distributor of aesthetic medical products and a provider of professional training for clinicians in the UK and Ireland. The company began as a pharmacy service in Guernsey and shifted its focus to aesthetic medical supplies in 2003. A significant milestone was the opening of its first UK pharmacy near Harley Street in 2005, followed by becoming the exclusive UK and Ireland supplier for Obagi Medical in 2006. 

The business operates by supplying medical professionals with a wide range of aesthetic products, including injectables, skincare, devices, and consumables from brands like Allergan, Obagi, and Medik8. Healthxchange generates revenue through the sale and distribution of these products, serving a client base of aesthetic medicine practitioners. In 2015, the firm launched an e-pharmacy service to broaden access for medical professionals across the nation. 

In addition to product distribution, the company established the Healthxchange Academy in 2010, which offers CPD-accredited training courses. These courses are conducted at facilities in Manchester, Reading, and Dublin, as well as online, covering topics such as botulinum toxin and dermal filler applications. The company also developed Clever Clinic in 2019, a patient management application designed to streamline clinical workflows. The current CEO is Jack Curran.

company.tagline: AI-powered event planning and coordination engine.
company.about: Pemberley Technology Limited, operating as Darcy, was co-founded in June 2026 by luxury wedding planner Hannah and software engineer Lotta. Darcy functions as an AI-driven event planning platform designed for weddings, private parties, corporate events, and curated trips. company.name: Frontier Computing
company.tagline: Scalable biological brains for ML training substrates.
company.about: Frontier Computing, founded in 2025 by Michael Domarkas and backed by Y Combinator, operates at the intersection of biotechnology and artificial intelligence. The company is developing scalable biological neural networks to serve as a substrate for machine learning training, addressing the high costs associated with training large parameter count models on traditional hardware. The core of Frontier's offering is a proprietary tissue-culture approach that overcomes the traditional limitations of in-vitro neuron scaling. While academic efforts have generally been confined to approximately 1 million neurons, Frontier has engineered a method to surpass this, with a pathway to scale to over 100 million neurons. This is achieved by solving the vascularization problem, which limits oxygen supply to cells in larger cultures. This technology collocates memory and compute at the substrate level, which enables the training of models with significantly larger parameter counts than what is tractable with conventional GPU architectures. Founder Michael Domarkas, a former Cambridge Natural Scientist, began culturing neuronal tissues with grant funding at the age of 17. His work led to the development of a scalable neuronal culture platform, which he validated by training a biological brain to play the game 'Frogger'. Frontier Computing is now focused on growing exascale biocomputing clusters. The company aims to launch a 500 million biological neuron cluster by January 2027. The company's business model involves providing the biological substrate, interfacing, and cloud infrastructure for third-party clients to train their machine learning models. This positions Frontier as a hardware and infrastructure provider in the biocomputing space, targeting entities that require highly efficient and cost-effective training for complex, long-horizon language reasoning and other advanced AI applications. company.name: London Quantum Group
company.tagline: Encrypted computation platform for healthcare data insights.
company.about: London Quantum Group (LQG) is a technology company focused on addressing a significant challenge in healthcare AI by enabling data analysis while maintaining stringent patient privacy. In August 2026, the company emerged from stealth with over $1.2 million in pre-seed funding from backers including Long Journey VC and healthcare angels. The company was established by Co-founder and CEO Sebastian Kot, who provides the mathematical and cryptographic vision, and Co-founder, COO, and CSO Dr. Chris Whittle, who contributes deep expertise in healthcare and governance from his previous roles as a UK and global Chief Medical Officer. Kot has a background that includes winning the NHS Hackathon and being recognized as a Top 100 Research Fellow by Bridgewater Associates. Dr. Whittle previously scaled essential online consultation technology during the COVID-19 pandemic and aims to remove data access bottlenecks that hinder medical innovation. LQG's core offering is the Blind Data Platform™, an infrastructure that facilitates encrypted computation on live, sensitive medical records. This technology allows for the generation of analytical insights and the training of machine learning models without the underlying data being viewed by third parties or leaving the custodianship of the data controller. The platform utilizes Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs) that are designed to exceed current regulatory standards, thus resolving the conflict between data security and its use for advanced research. In the United Kingdom, the company's technology is applied through its research and clinician-facing product, Provenance™, to support insights and model training within the National Health Service (NHS). In the United States, the platform is used to securely process Electronic Medical Records for clinical insights and to train sophisticated AI models for applications like cancer prediction. company.tagline: AI-powered solutions to sort recyclable materials
company.about:
SortedTech.io is a forward-thinking startup focused on revolutionizing the waste management industry through advanced technology. Founded by Arthur and Luis, who collectively bring over 25 years of experience in waste management, operations, and technology, the company aims to tackle the global plastic waste crisis. Every minute, one million plastic bottles are purchased, and up to five trillion plastic bags are used annually worldwide. Half of all plastic produced is for single-use purposes, which means it is used once and then discarded. SortedTech.io addresses this issue by developing AI-powered solutions that help waste management companies sort recyclable materials more efficiently.

The company's primary product is an AI-driven system that sorts recyclable plastics at a very detailed level, distinguishing between different types of resin and usage. This granular sorting capability meets the stringent requirements of the recycling industry, helping to reduce the amount of recyclable material that ends up in landfills or incineration. By improving sorting efficiency, SortedTech.io enables waste management companies to maximize the amount of material that can be recycled, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability.

SortedTech.io operates in the waste management and recycling market, serving primarily B2B (business-to-business) clients. These clients include waste management companies that are looking to enhance their recycling processes and reduce operational inefficiencies. The business model is likely based on a combination of software licensing and service fees, where clients pay for access to the AI-powered sorting technology and possibly for ongoing support and updates.

Revenue is generated through these licensing agreements and service contracts, providing a steady stream of income as waste management companies continuously seek to improve their recycling capabilities. The company's focus on leveraging AI technology to solve real-world problems positions it well in a market that is increasingly prioritizing sustainability and efficiency.

company.tagline: Creator subscription platform that empowers creators to connect, create and earn with their fans
company.about:
Fanvue is a subscription-based social platform designed to empower creators by providing them with a space to share content, earn money, and connect with their fans. The platform caters to a diverse range of creators, including influencers, adult content creators, athletes, and artists. Fanvue operates in the digital content creation market, which has seen significant growth as more individuals seek to monetize their online presence.

The business model of Fanvue revolves around subscription fees and content sales. Creators can set up profiles and offer exclusive content to their fans for a subscription fee. Fanvue takes a commission from these earnings, allowing creators to keep 85% of their revenue for the first three months and 80% thereafter. This model incentivizes creators to join and stay on the platform, as they retain a significant portion of their earnings.

Fanvue makes money by taking a percentage of the revenue generated by creators. This includes subscription fees paid by fans and any additional content sales. The platform's appeal lies in its relatively high payout rates and the promise of minimal censorship, which can be a significant draw for creators who have faced restrictions on other platforms.

The platform also emphasizes ease of use, allowing creators to become verified and start earning in less than three minutes. Earnings can be withdrawn as soon as they hit the creator's balance, providing quick access to funds. This user-friendly approach, combined with the potential for high earnings, makes Fanvue an attractive option for content creators looking to monetize their work.

Fanvue also takes data privacy seriously, adhering to legal obligations regarding the processing and protection of personal data. Users have rights to access information about how their data is used and can opt out of marketing messages at any time.

company.tagline: BILRS is a global B2B bill payment platform that enables companies to integrate and offer a wide range of bill payment options through a single API or SDK
company.about:
BILRS, founded in 2022 by CEO Rupert Shaw, operates as a global bill payment platform targeting the financial technology sector. The company is headquartered in Nottingham, United Kingdom, with a corporate office in Dubai, UAE, positioning itself within key financial hubs. As a venture-backed seed-stage company, BILRS has secured funding from institutional investors, including Haatch and Spring Studios, through funding rounds in September 2023 and March 2025.

The core of BILRS's business is a B2B model that provides a technology platform for financial institutions, remittance operators, and retail entities. Clients integrate BILRS's powerful API or SDK, which is designed to be adaptable to any technology stack, to offer a vast selection of global bill payment services to their own customer base. This single-integration solution allows end-users to pay for utilities like power and gas, among thousands of other bill types, across multiple continents. The business generates revenue by enabling these transactions, helping its clients to lower customer acquisition costs, create new revenue streams, and improve user engagement through the recurring nature of bill payments.

The company's platform is designed to handle the complexities of compliance, regulation, and scale in a standardized manner for its partners. By connecting to the BILRS system, merchants can seamlessly process global bill payments. The platform's value proposition is centered on simplifying cross-border payments and enhancing the service offerings of its clients. This is exemplified by strategic partnerships with firms like Al Ansari Exchange and Bayfikr to revolutionize bill management for expatriates in the UK and UAE. In recognition of its early-stage growth, BILRS was named the Equity Backed Start-Up Award Winner at the 2024 Midlands Startup Awards.

company.name: ClearPath AI
company.tagline: AI operating system for professional services workflows.
company.about:
ClearPath AI is a UK-based fintech company developing an AI-native operating system to automate and connect workflows across the legal, property, mortgage, and financial services sectors. The venture was founded by technology entrepreneur Rudi Kesic, who previously founded and exited a legal technology company. Kesic, who has over 25 years of experience in legal services and technology, launched ClearPath AI in Birmingham with £1 million in pre-seed funding. 

The company's core product, ClearPathOS, is an operating system built with AI at its architectural core, designed to work alongside existing business software rather than requiring replacement of legacy systems. It targets professional sectors where significant time is spent on manual document review, data interpretation, and inter-organizational communication. ClearPathOS features four specialized products: Finance AI, Property AI, Legal AI, and Compliance AI, which can be used independently or together. 

For the mortgage industry, Finance AI assists brokers by managing cases from fact-finding and affordability assessments to application packaging and completion. It can analyze payslips, review bank statements, chase missing documents, and match cases against lender criteria. For legal and property professionals, the platform supports client communication, document handling, and sales progression. A key feature of the system is its ability to create a connected ecosystem where, with permission, authorized information can flow between estate agents, mortgage brokers, lenders, and lawyers, reducing data re-entry and delays. This aims to streamline the home-moving process for consumers, who often have to repeatedly provide the same information to different parties. 

ClearPath AI's business model is based on providing its AI-native platform to professional services firms to reduce administrative burdens and enhance efficiency. The company is headquartered commercially in Birmingham, UK, with its technology and engineering operations based in Ljubljana, Slovenia.

company.tagline: AI-powered evaluation of investment strategy track records
company.about:
Atlas Quant provides a platform for allocators and investors to evaluate the performance and authenticity of investment strategies. It uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to run forensic diagnostics on track records, assess their robustness, and identify predictive edges. The service is designed to standardize strategy evaluation across various asset classes, including digital assets, equities, FX, and macro strategies. 

The company, originally founded as Atlas Quantitative Systems (AQS) in 2023 at the Inospring Incubator in Silicon Valley, was officially incorporated as AQS Limited in 2024. The initial project was launched under the name Atlas Quantitative Lab in 2024. By 2025, the firm had secured a $20 million angel funding round led by the Numeraai Foundation and established Singapore as its Asia-Pacific hub. 

The founding team includes Ernest P. Chan, an author and expert in quantitative trading, who serves as the founder responsible for overall strategy. Co-founder Richard Craib, founder of the machine learning hedge fund Numerai, provided early funding and resources. The platform's clients can upload any strategy or track record, and the system generates scores on risk, robustness, and forward potential to aid in selection and allocation decisions. Atlas Quant also runs trading competitions for professional traders to accumulate decision-making data and refine its AI models.

company.name: Twyne Labs
company.tagline: AI-powered sales training through role-play simulations.
company.about:
Twyne Labs is a technology company specializing in artificial intelligence-driven sales training solutions. The firm provides a platform where sales representatives can practice and refine their skills through realistic, AI-powered role-play simulations. These simulations cover various sales scenarios, including cold calls, discovery meetings, and handling objections, allowing for tailored practice sessions that match a company's specific buyer personas and sales processes. 

The platform's core feature, RolePlayAI, enables sellers to engage in real-time text and audio conversations with an AI counterpart that realistically simulates buyer behaviors and concerns. This provides a safe environment for representatives to prepare for customer interactions without the risk of losing deals. Following these practice sessions, the system delivers immediate, consistent feedback and coaching. It includes an 'AI speech coach' that provides suggestions on sentence structure, pacing, and eliminating filler words, functioning similarly to a grammar-checker for sales conversations. This allows for scalable coaching and skill development without overburdening sales managers, who can often be a bottleneck in traditional training. 

Twyne Labs's business model is centered on improving sales team performance, with stated goals of decreasing onboarding time and accelerating proficiency attainment. The training modules can be integrated into broader enablement programs, such as onboarding courses, product launch training, and leadership coaching, to increase knowledge retention and engagement. The platform offers templates for various sales methodologies like SPIN, MEDDPICC, and BANT, and also allows for full customization.

company.name: IntusHQ
company.tagline: Asset management software for UHNWI portfolios.
company.about: IntusHQ offers a mobile-first, centralized software platform for managing high-value assets for Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individuals (UHNWIs), family offices, and their operational teams. The company targets the complexities of managing globally distributed portfolios, which often rely on fragmented spreadsheets and institutional knowledge that is lost with staff turnover. It operates as a SaaS business, providing its platform to clients such as estate managers, yacht crew, and family offices to oversee assets across multiple properties, yachts, and collections. Founded by Katy Jeffcoate, the company stems from her direct experience in the luxury sector. Jeffcoate spent over 25 years managing luxury yachts, consulting on new builds, and overseeing operations for UHNW families. During this time, she identified a gap in the market for a system designed to manage interior inventories—such as furniture, artwork, wine collections, and jewellery—which were tracked using inadequate methods like spreadsheets. This insight led to the creation of IntusHQ, a platform built to provide a holistic view of personal inventories across a family's entire portfolio. The company's team includes Leslie Gillotte as Operations and Growth Lead, who brings commercial expertise from her time co-founding Pinpoint Works, a yacht management software platform that was acquired by Voly in 2023. In August 2026, IntusHQ secured a six-figure investment to accelerate product development and scale customer acquisition. One of the investors is Craig Hopwood, the former CFO of Voly, adding financial and operational experience from the yachting technology sector to the company. The IntusHQ platform allows users to create a unified catalogue of all assets, from furniture and artwork to vehicles and consumables, across every property and storage location. Each item has a detailed profile that can store photos, purchase details, provenance, documentation, and care instructions. Key features include inventory movement tracking, photo-based cataloging, custom categories, and role-based permissions for different team members. The platform is designed to provide real-time transparency, reduce the risk of loss or damage, and ensure that information is centralized and accessible to authorized personnel. The system is currently in real-world testing and is being developed with direct input from its user base as part of an early adoption program. company.tagline: Compare CS2 skin prices across marketplaces
company.about:
SkinScanner.gg, formerly known as MaestroAI, is a UK-based price comparison platform for Counter-Strike 2 skins. Operated by Maestro AI Ltd, it aggregates live listings across dozens of third-party marketplaces so players and traders can see where a skin is cheapest to buy or most valuable to sell—without SkinScanner holding skins, Steam logins, or funds.

company.name: Metal Morph
company.tagline: Circular recovery of water treatment coagulants.
company.about: Metal Morph is a climate tech company focused on advancing sustainability and efficiency within the water industry by implementing circular economy processes. The firm was founded by Moletsane Mophethe (CEO), an inventor and award recipient from the Royal Academy of Engineering and the World Bank, and Thomas Jacks (CCO), who has 14 years of experience in the water sector, including a role as Head of Dealflow at Isle Utilities. They are joined by a team that includes Dr. Grace Anne Lowe as Head of Science and Devni Acharya as Chief of Staff. The company addresses the water industry's push towards net-zero commitments by offering a solution to reduce costs, carbon emissions, and supply chain risks associated with water treatment. Metal Morph's primary clients are water and wastewater utilities. The business operates on an infrastructure-as-a-service model, integrating its technology directly into existing treatment facilities. This approach eliminates the need for major capital expenditure from the client, reduces operational disruption, and mitigates technical risk. Metal Morph has developed a patent-pending process that recovers and reuses spent metal-based water treatment chemicals, specifically coagulants like aluminum sulfate and iron chloride. The process involves four key stages: extraction of the waste sludge through acid leaching, selective separation using Donnan dialysis, reactivation via membrane processes and purification, and finally the return of the high-purity coagulant for reuse. The company reports a recovery rate of 90% with 95% purity for the recovered coagulants, which can lead to an 89% reduction in associated CO2 emissions. In 2023, the company secured an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from investors including Orbit Ventures and SOSV. company.name: FlairMakers
company.tagline: On-demand talent and compliance platform for hospitality.
company.about: FlairMakers operates a talent-as-a-service platform built for the hospitality industry, connecting businesses with vetted freelance professionals for temporary engagements. The company provides an infrastructure layer that manages the entire freelance workflow, including training, compliance, contracts, and same-day payments, targeting the operational inefficiencies of traditional staffing models. It aims to formalize the freelance or 'portfolio career' path for hospitality workers, providing a system for what often runs on informal networks. The company was founded by CEO Raluca Epureanu and CTO Alexis Sikorsky, who met during an executive MBA program at Oxford's Saïd Business School. Epureanu brings 20 years of global hospitality experience, having previously run the regional events division for Marriott International in Asia Pacific, where she was responsible for 750 hotels. This experience informed her vision to build a platform she wished had existed in the industry. Sikorsky is a serial entrepreneur who previously built and exited a banking software business in a nine-figure transaction. His background is in creating infrastructure for regulated industries, a lesson he applies to solving the compliance and payment complexities of freelance talent management. FlairMakers' business model is a B2B service that treats both hospitality venues and freelance talent as businesses. For its clients—hotels, restaurants, and event operators—the platform reduces administrative overhead and recruitment costs by providing on-demand access to a pre-screened talent pool. It offers access to professionals across three tiers: operational (e.g., bartenders, chefs), management (e.g., event managers), and executive/consultancy roles. The platform is live in the UK and Romania. In August 2026, FlairMakers announced it had closed a £500,000 pre-seed funding round led by SFC Capital to fund product development and expand its UK venue network. The company was also named Hospitality, Tourism & Events StartUp of the Year at the 2026 London UK StartUp Awards. company.name: Vitalis Ortho
company.tagline: Regenerative implant device for knee osteoarthritis treatment.
company.about: Vitalis Ortho is a London-based medical device company founded in 2025 to address a significant treatment gap in knee osteoarthritis care. The company was established by Olly Morgan and Mac Tuncer, who both hold PhDs in biomechanics and knee replacement. Their previous venture involved scaling Meshworks Implants into a leading provider of personalized, 3D-printed orthopedic implants in the UK and Ireland, which they successfully exited in 2024. This experience provided them with deep insights into the shortcomings of the patient journey for joint conditions, particularly for younger patients. The company targets the market of over 365 million people globally with knee osteoarthritis, focusing specifically on the 37% of patients under 65. This demographic often finds themselves in a difficult position: considered too young for a total knee replacement due to the high lifetime revision risk, yet experiencing significant pain that is not adequately managed by conservative treatments. Vitalis Ortho aims to fill this void by making joint preservation the standard of care for this patient group. Vitalis Ortho is developing a temporary, surgically implantable device that promotes cartilage regeneration. This regenerative intervention is designed to delay or potentially prevent the need for a full joint replacement surgery. The business model is centered on the development and commercialization of this therapeutic device. In June 2026, the company secured £1.2 million in an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round. The round was co-led by venture capital firm Zinc and Aligned Syndicate, with participation from Orthopaedic Research UK, Innovate UK Growth Catalyst, and a group of angel investors that includes orthopedic surgeons. This capital is being used to fund device testing and early preclinical validation, moving the product closer to first-in-human trials. It uses sophisticated lighting, sound, and visual effects to create a multi-sensory, show-like experience. company.name: Neutonic
company.tagline: Nootropic beverages for enhanced focus and productivity
company.about:
Neutonic is a beverage and supplement brand that produces nootropic drinks, powders, and capsules designed to improve cognitive function, focus, and productivity without the negative effects associated with traditional energy drinks. The company was founded in November 2023 by influencers James Smith, a personal trainer known for his evidence-based approach to fitness, and Chris Williamson, host of the 'Modern Wisdom' podcast, along with manager Luke Betts and Genflow CEO Shan Hanif. The founders identified a gap in the market for a sugar-free, productivity-focused drink with research-backed ingredients. Smith, a consumer of energy drinks himself, and Williamson, a self-described connoisseur, were deeply involved in the formulation to create a product that offered sustained energy and focus without jitters or a subsequent crash. 

The company's business model is direct-to-consumer (DTC), selling its products through its website, Amazon, and TikTok Shop in the UK and US. Its target market includes health-conscious individuals and those seeking mindful alternatives to coffee and sugary energy drinks. Since its launch, Neutonic has sold over three million cans and generated more than $10 million in revenue, achieving a number one ranking on Amazon in the energy drink and grocery categories. In July 2025, the company secured $3.7 million in a seed funding round, reaching a valuation of $20 million. The investment was supported by a group of high-profile entrepreneurs and influencers, including Grenade founder Alan Barratt and fitness entrepreneur Kayla Itsines. This capital is intended to fuel expansion into UK and US retail markets, scale the workforce, and support new product development. 

Neutonic's flagship product is its 'Productivity Drink', which contains a blend of nootropic ingredients such as Cognizin, Rhodiola Rosea, Panax Ginseng, and L-Theanine, combined with 120mg of natural caffeine and B vitamins. The brand also offers caffeine-free alternatives, including 'Brain Capsules' and a powdered 'Focus Blend'. The product line is available in several flavors, including Tropical Ice, Orange Sunrise, and Wild Citrus.

company.name: Evorra
company.tagline: Easiest way to curate, control, and activate addressable audiences at scale
company.about:
Evorra operates as a SaaS-based data marketplace, addressing the advertising technology sector's shift away from third-party cookies. Founded in December 2020 by Aaron Ritoper, Warren Chang, and Piero Poli, the London-headquartered company provides a platform for brands and agencies to build and activate audiences using privacy-compliant, first-party data. The founding team's collective background in data, ad-tech, and media, with experience at companies like HP, Amadeus, Skyscanner, Sojern, and Deloitte, shaped Evorra's mission to simplify data-driven marketing for non-technical professionals. 

The company's business model centers on providing tools for two main client types: data owners (like publishers) and data users (brands and agencies). Data owners can monetize their opted-in audience data with full transparency and control, tracking usage and revenue through a dedicated dashboard. For brands and agencies, Evorra offers a self-service platform to build custom audiences from a global pool of data partners without needing complex integrations or engineering resources. The platform is designed to be user-friendly, allowing marketers to create and deploy targetable audiences in minutes, with control over the cost per thousand impressions (CPM) to manage budgets effectively. 

Evorra's core service is its Audience Intelligence Platform, which leverages clean-room technology to unify fragmented data signals into stable, privacy-first user profiles. This allows for the creation of addressable audiences that are not reliant on cookies, making them suitable for activation across various digital channels, including CTV, audio, and gaming. Key features include detailed audience segmentation, transparent data sourcing, and an intelligent identity resolution engine that links diverse user identifiers and attributes like intent and demographics. By April 2023, the platform had integrated over half a billion cookieless audience profiles, with a significant data presence in the US, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Strategic partnerships, such as one with identity provider ID5, further enhance its capability to deliver scalable, privacy-compliant audience targeting.

company.name: Alfred
company.tagline: Wholesale household utilities via annual membership.
company.about: Alfred operates as a membership-based household services provider in the United Kingdom, consolidating energy, mobile, broadband, and insurance services. The company's business model is centered on a fixed annual membership fee of £195, which grants customers access to these essential home services at wholesale prices. This structure, inspired by Costco, allows Alfred to generate revenue from memberships rather than adding profit margins to the services used by its members. The platform serves as the single point of contact for all billing and support inquiries. The company leverages generative AI to maintain a lean operating model, which helps in passing savings directly to its members. Alfred partners with major wholesalers, including British Gas for energy and providers like Aviva and AXA for its insurance panel. company.name: Safehire.ai
company.tagline: AI-powered deep web background checks for recruitment
company.about:
Safehire.ai is a UK-based technology company providing AI-powered background screening services that scan deep and dark web sources to identify risks in potential and current employees. The company was co-founded by Simon Holden (CEO) and Sean Lumley (COO), two former British Army officers who met at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst over two decades ago. Holden has a background as a senior leader in UK education and founded a cybersecurity company, CyBur, while Lumley also has a history in security and risk management. Safehire.ai was incorporated on January 29, 2024, and officially launched its platform in July 2025 at the Independent Schools’ Bursars Conference.

The company's core service utilizes a proprietary AI search engine named 'Echo', developed by former military intelligence analysts, which is combined with a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) analysis to validate findings. This process scans billions of open-source data points to uncover risks such as radicalization, extremist links, and hate speech that traditional Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks might miss. The service is designed to be compliant with UK regulations, including the KCSIE (Keeping Children Safe in Education) guidance.

Safehire.ai operates on a B2B Software as a Service (SaaS) business model, primarily targeting regulated sectors like education, healthcare, youth organizations, and other industries where trust and safety are paramount. Its revenue is generated through an annual subscription model where clients purchase prepaid plans of background check reports. Pricing per report ranges from approximately £20 to £30, depending on the subscription volume, with options for pay-as-you-go top-ups and priority 24-hour report turnarounds. Reports are typically delivered within three days.

company.name: Reimagine Robotics
company.tagline: AI platform for on-the-job robot training.
company.about: Reimagine Robotics is developing an artificial intelligence platform that enables workers to train industrial robots directly on the factory floor without specialized programming knowledge. The company was founded in April 2025 by CEO Jonathan Scholz, Oleg Sushkov, Akhil Raju, and Misha Denil, all former leaders from Google DeepMind's Applied Robotics team. The founding team combines expertise in imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and real-world robot manipulation to bridge the gap between advanced robotics and practical field applications. The firm's core technology is a software interface for vision-enabled collaborative robots that allows operators to teach tasks through demonstration. This process, which the company calls 'monkey-see, monkey-do,' involves a worker showing the robot a task, observing its attempt, and making immediate corrections. This approach drastically reduces the time needed to prototype and test new robot behaviors from days to as little as ten minutes. The system is designed to amplify human labor, not replace it, by allowing employees to identify production bottlenecks and deploy robots to handle repetitive or tedious physical tasks. With headquarters in London and Sydney, Reimagine Robotics emerged from stealth in August 2026 after securing an undisclosed amount of pre-seed financing from investors including Fly Ventures and firstminute capital. The company is targeting the advanced manufacturing and electronics disassembly sectors. Early deployments include training robots to tend 3D printers and creating a multi-robot cell for recovering valuable materials from used hard drives. The business model focuses on making automation more accessible and adaptable for low-volume or variable workflows, enabling client teams to expand automation to new processes independently. company.tagline: An app-linked debit card, allowing users to spend, budget, and save with full knowledge of where money is all times
company.about:
Kestrl is a financial technology company targeting the specific needs of Muslim consumers by offering services that facilitate wealth growth in accordance with their beliefs. The company was established in London in 2019 by Areeb Siddiqui and Daeng Termizi, who met while pursuing their MBAs at the University of Cambridge. Their journey began after identifying a significant gap in the market; a survey they conducted revealed that over 90% of Muslims felt dissatisfied with the available financial options that aligned with their faith. Siddiqui, now CEO, brought his experience in management consulting at PwC and Deloitte, where he focused on fintech solutions for banks. Termizi, the COO, contributed his background as an analyst at the Central Bank of Malaysia, specializing in Islamic finance. 

Kestrl operates on a dual model, providing a direct-to-consumer application and a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution for banks. The consumer app utilizes open banking to consolidate a user's bank accounts, offering a holistic view of their finances. Key features include budgeting tools, goal-oriented savings pots, bill tracking, and a marketplace for Sharia-compliant investment products like gold and property. The app is Sharia-compliant, a status monitored and certified by Amanah Advisors, which ensures investments avoid sectors such as alcohol, gambling, and weapons, and that no interest is charged. For its B2B clients, Kestrl offers white-label solutions that banks can integrate into their own platforms to better serve their Muslim customers. This includes tools for personal financial management, Zakat calculation, and Shariah-compliant stock screening. The company has formed partnerships with institutions like Bank Islam in Malaysia and Emirates Islamic Bank in the UAE. 

The company's revenue model is multifaceted, incorporating a freemium subscription structure for the app, commissions from third-party providers on its marketplace, and monthly fees from its B2B SaaS clients. Since its inception, Kestrl has raised approximately $254K through several seed funding rounds, with investors including Techstars and the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC). The company was also part of the Accelerate Cambridge program, which provided crucial mentorship. With a tech team based in Malaysia, Kestrl is focused on expanding its services and market reach, aiming for operational profitability by 2025.

company.name: OLIX
company.tagline: Optical compute infrastructure for frontier AI
company.about: OLIX (formerly Flux) is a London-based AI chip company founded in 2024 that builds optical compute infrastructure for frontier AI inference. It designs chips, lasers and interconnects so each stage of token generation can run on specialised hardware rather than the same general-purpose GPU. Its X-1 platform unrolls models across many chips with a slow-and-wide optical interconnect and a deterministic compiler; DX-1 is the first decode accelerator, holding models in on-chip SRAM without advanced packaging or HBM. In August 2026 OLIX raised a €270.5 million ($312 million) Series B at a €2.8 billion ($3.3 billion) valuation, with Fundomo, Arm and Hudson River Trading joining alongside angels including Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings, while existing investors increased commitments. Professor Nick McKeown joined the board and former Wise executive Matt Briers became CFO. Proceeds fund DX-1 delivery to first customers by H2 2027 and manufacturing scale-up, with hiring in London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco. Sources: EU-Startups 3 Aug 2026; olix.com.
